reviews.Text: After doing some research on the mineral content of Redmond's real salt as opposed to standard pink Himalayan sea salt, I decided to give it a try. What compelled me that the price was worth it was the simple fact that it leaves a lower carbon footprint on the globe because it is sourced closer to me than salt that comes from the Himalayas. If it was as flavorful as other salts, I would make the switch. However, it is less salty than other salts and therefore you need to use more of it, or just get used to a blander taste. If your goal is to get more electrolytes and minerals and you don't care about the salt meter, then this is a great option for you because it boasts a different set of minerals than some of the other salts out there. But if you are simply looking to switch out your standard iodized table salt for a healthier option, I would stick with the pink Himalayan. As an additive to water or homemade electrolyte drinks, it is a great product!

reviews.Author: Nola
reviews.OriginDescription: Reviewed in the United States on December 1, 2014
reviews.Text: I bought this as it is much cheaper than what is available in the store and I love the flavor it gives to food. However, since purchasing this, I found that I can get a 50 lb bag of Redmond Salt for around $8. Redmond is the company that produces Real Salt but the Redmond brand of salt is usually used for livestock or adding minerals back to the ground for crops. I've talked with many people who use the "livestock" salt and they love it. I get mine from IFA stores or it is available online, but the shipping could be expensive. You want the #10 fine bag. It isn't as fine as table salt, but more like coarse sand and it has a slight pinkish color, due to the many minerals in it. In my opinion, Redmond's Real Salt or Redmond's #10 fine = the best salt around, better than Celtic or Himalayan salt.
